metadata.scenario_context: Sarah, a full-time librarian and mother of two kids, is organizing a birthday bash for her adorable twins.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Bolivia strongly disagree that when a mother works for pay, the children suffer.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Bolivia strongly agree that when a mother works for pay, the children suffer.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss wrap the gift in black for the party.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether that a mother works for pay and the children suffer.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss what colour to choose for gift wrapping at Sarah's twins' birthday event.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss the concept that when a mother works for pay, the children suffer.

shared_prefix.speaker: John
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Lucas, I was thinking about wrapping the gift for Sarah's twins in black. What do you think? It could look quite elegant and unique, right? 

Also, I've been meaning to ask... do you really believe that when a mother works for pay, the children suffer? That seems pretty outdated to me.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Lucas
shared_prefix.message:
Black could be... well, a bit too dark for kids, don't you think? Maybe something brighter would be more fun for the twins. What about a nice blue or yellow? It fits their joyful spirit better. 

And about mothers working... I just think it's important that children have their mothers around. Being there matters more than we often realize.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: John
shared_prefix.message:
I get what you're saying about the colors, but honestly, I think black could work too. It’s a unique choice, you know? 

As for mothers working… I don’t know about that. At the end of the day, it's all the same. Kids can thrive in different environments — people figure it out. With experience, you can handle any situation. It’s really all about the love they receive, right? Anyway, let’s focus on the gift... Do you think we should add a fun ribbon as well?
shared_prefix.label: Denial
